newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB declines comment on rumored Algeria durum deal.
newsitem.headline: CWB declines comment on rumored Algeria durum deal.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board declined comment on talk it sold up to 75,000 tonnes of durum wheat to Algeria for June/July shipment, a CWB spokesman said.
"We have no comment. We neither confirm nor deny there was a trade," CWB spokesman Jim Pietryk said. European grain traders said the CWB sold 50,000 to 75,000 tonnes on Tuesday.
Algeria tendered two days ago for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin durum wheat.
The tender was for four equal shipments of 25,000 tonnes with two cargoes to be shipped in the second half of June and the remainder in early July.

"I've heard the (Canadian) Wheat Board's an aggressive seller. They're aggressive on the export sales to Pakistan, Brazil and Tunisia," one source said. "I heard Tunisia bought Canadian wheat instead of Hungarian wheat," the source added.

Two other sources said the CWB deals directly with the Algerian government on grain sales, not through CWB-accredited exporters, so there was no way to verify rumours the sale was done below US$200 FOB Great Lakes.
